transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-04 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Miles (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Aisha (NimbusLedger), Connor (NimbusPlatform), Lina (SRE), Diego (PM)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be noisy): Redwood and NimbusLedger scoped a pilot to validate inference economics and latency SLOs for a conversational payments assistant. Customer will share obfuscated traffic; Redwood will produce benchmark plan with QPS/concurrency bands and success criteria. Focus on tail latency, token mix, and caching opportunities.

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh quick roll call, then we'll get into scope.
[00:10] Aisha: yep hi, that's Aisha here. trying to keep this short, we have a tight timeline - looking for a pilot in october.
[00:15] Sofia: got it - timeline noted. Miles, do you want to frame the technical goals?
[00:20] Miles: yeah hi all. the goal for the POC from our side is threefold: one, reproduce a slice of your production traffic to validate p95/p99 latency at target load; two, measure cost per 1M tokens and identify batching/caching levers; three, validate fallbacks — e.g. smaller quantized model or lower-tier region — while staying within SLA.
[00:40] Connor: sounds good. our big unknown is concurrency shape — we get steady-state qps of about 30rps for the assistant, but we see spikes to 250rps during peak campaigns. those spikes are short (30s-2m) but very frequent.
[01:05] Miles: ok that's useful. can you confirm average input token length and response tokens? like are queries short (10-30 tokens) or long?
[01:12] Aisha: there is a skew - 60% of requests are short (single-sentence intents, 8-20 tokens), 30% are medium (40-80 tokens with context), 10% are long (200+ tokens for multi-turn summaries). response size varies, typical reply is 32-120 tokens, but long flows hit ~400 tokens occasionally.
[01:40] Lina: and we have KV cache we keep per-conversation, but we don't persist across reboots - it's in our app layer. sometimes the se transciption shows it as K V cache.
[01:52] Ravi: heh yeah, transcription quirks noted. for sizing we need two main numbers from you: qps distribution histogram (1s buckets ideal) and concurrency distribution (how many active sessions hold the kv cache concurrently).
[02:10] Diego: we can provide p95 latencies from our current vendor but the payload shapes are what's important for you, right?
[02:15] Miles: correct. also we want a sample of the prompt categories so we can parameterize the benchmark (e.g., single-turn transfer intent vs multi-turn verification vs summary).
[02:25] Aisha: we'll sanitize and send that. security note: any retained logs must be encrypted at rest and we need KMS integration if you host.
[02:33] Sofia: noted. we'll include the security pack; we support KMS and have SOC2 certs - I'll attach those.
[02:40] Connor: deployment question: are you recommending Redwood Hosted or Dedicated for this workload? cost/latency tradeoffs?
[02:48] Miles: short answer: start with Hosted to reduce friction for the first replay/bench. if the spikes/throughput drive unit economics or you need network isolation, Dedicated is the next step. we will quantify both in the benchmark plan.
[03:05] Aisha: for the SLA, our product team wants p95 < 250ms for short queries and p95 < 600ms for medium/long. p99 targets are negotiable but we'd like to understand tail behavior.
[03:18] Ravi: those are reasonable. we'll design benchmark phases: baseline single-request latency (no batching), then production-replay at steady qps, then spike replay to exercise burst capacity, and finally long-response throughput for token-heavy flows.
[03:35] Miles: we should also capture time-to-first-byte for streaming vs end-to-end generation. streaming helps perceived latency for long responses.
[03:45] Aisha: do you have guidance on autoscaling units? we run on k8s for other services and prefer to know how many GPUs we should expect.
[03:55] Miles: rough back-of-envelope: for a Llama-like 13B with quantization and optimized kernels, you might get ~25–40 qps per A100-like instance for 128/64 token exchanges, but that varies. for short 20-token inputs and 64-token replies, effective tokens/sec matters more. we'll give ranges once we analyze your token mix.
[04:20] Connor: what about batching impact on latency for short requests? we care about tail.
[04:25] Miles: batching increases throughput but can add latency for small real-time queries. our optimizer chooses per-route batching windows; for low-latency routes we keep batch windows small (5–25ms) and rely on prefix caching. we'll measure this during the baseline tests.
[04:45] Diego: what metrics will you provide after each phase?
[04:48] Ravi: p50/p95/p99 token-latency, tokens/sec, tokens/cost, throughput (rps), concurrency histogram, GPU utilization, memory footprints, and failure/retry rates. we'll also estimate $/1M tokens under the observed batch configs.
[05:05] Aisha: timeline — you said you'll have a plan by next week? we need it to sync with procurement.
[05:11] Sofia: yes I'll share a preliminary benchmark plan by Sep 6, a final runbook by Sep 9, and then we'd like to run the replay the week of Sep 14 if that works for you.
[05:25] Aisha: week of Sep 14 works. procurement wants an initial quote for both Hosted and Dedicated.
[05:31] Sofia: we'll include a pricing band in the security pack.
[05:35] [06:00] (short side conversations and crosstalk about internal calendars)
[06:40] Connor: on replay, do you need actual audio/heavy content or just the text prompts? we do conversion from IVR to text; some noise in transcripts.
[06:48] Miles: text alone is fine for model sizing; audio path doesn't change token dynamics except transcription artifacts. provide the final prompts your app sends to the model after any pre-processing.
[07:05] Aisha: one more nuance — we do user-specific signals in the prompt (recent transactions) that can add 200–600 tokens per prompt in some verification flows. those are highly cacheable per-session.
[07:22] Miles: that helps; we'll look for opportunities to KV-cache static pieces of context and to use prefix caching to cut redundant tokens. please tag sample flows that are heavy with user signals.
[07:35] Lina: network isolation question: if we go Dedicated with VPC peering, do you support private control plane?
[07:42] Ravi: yes we have Redwood Private offering with customer-managed networking and optional on-prem connectors. we'll include the architecture diagram in the security pack.
[07:55] Diego: curious — in the benchmark runbook will you include canary/fallback policies? we want to simulate graceful degradation when capacity is exhausted.
[08:05] Miles: absolutely — one of the tests will force a model fallback to a smaller quantized variant and measure quality delta by a tiny set of eval prompts you provide.
[08:18] Aisha: about evals — we'll need to see quality metrics, rouge/bleu won't cut it for us, we prefer task-success rate (e.g., verification accepted by downstream service).
[08:28] Miles: that's fine; include a small set of golden prompts with expected outcomes. we'll produce a simple pass/fail metric plus confidence histograms.
[08:40] (silence while notes taken)
[09:00] Sofia: quick question for procurement: do you have any regulatory constraints for data residency?
[09:06] Aisha: data must remain in us-east for regional customers, but some customers require eu residency; our pilot will be us-east.
[09:14] Sofia: ok we'll note regional routing and fallbacks.
[09:20] Connor: about benchmarks — can you run both streaming and non-streaming modes? we want to compare perceived latency.
[09:28] Miles: yes we'll run TTFB and full-response aggregates for both modes.
[09:35] Diego: what about concurrency per-session? we sometimes hold 3 concurrent model calls per session during verification.
[09:42] Ravi: we'll synthesize concurrency profiles in the replay harness; please include max concurrent session counts per minute in your export.
[09:50] Aisha: who will own the replay orchestration? we prefer Redwood to run initial runs in Hosted with sanitized traffic, then a joint run in Dedicated if we move forward.
[09:58] Miles: Redwood can orchestrate the first three phases in Hosted; if you want Dedicated we'll run step four with your network team.
[10:08] Aisha: perfect. can you remind us what success criteria look like?
[10:12] Miles: sure, we'll codify final success criteria but draft version: 1) p95 latency within client targets for at least 95% of steady-state traffic; 2) end-to-end throughput to support average qps plus n-sigma spikes (we'll define sigma after traffic histogram); 3) cost per 1M tokens within the pricing band you accept; 4) fallback behavior maintains 85% task-success for degraded variants.
[10:35] Sofia: and acceptance test: joint run with obfuscated traffic where both sides validate latency and quality; if passed, we go into a 30-day pilot with monthly billing estimate.
[10:48] Aisha: ok, procurement will need the quote and security docs before Sep 10 to keep the procurement window.
[11:00] Sofia: noted - I'll push docs earlier.
[11:06] (small tangential conversation about metrics naming and instrumentation)
[11:30] Connor: question: do you support per-route SLAs? we have some high-priority routes and low-priority ones.
[11:36] Ravi: yes, Redwood supports per-route policies - you can set latency SLOs and separate batching profiles. we'll recommend tiering in the plan.
[11:48] Aisha: any standard test harness you use? can we run it ourselves?
[11:53] Miles: we provide a replay harness and a set of runners (k6 + custom token-aware driver). we'll give instructions to run locally or in your infra.
[12:05] Diego: last thing — can you include an estimate of token retention and log retention costs?
[12:10] Sofia: yes included in the pricing appendix.
[12:15] (wrap-up)
[12:25] Miles: recap of actions: Redwood will send benchmark plan + runbook link (sheet), security pack, preliminary pricing band. NimbusLedger provides sanitized traffic, golden eval prompts, concurrency histograms. target: Redwood deliver final runbook by Sep 9, run initial Hosted replay week of Sep 14.
[12:50] Aisha: sounds good, thanks.
[12:55] Sofia: thanks everyone, sending notes and next steps after the call.
